description: A study of what a constitution is, its types, importance and supremacy, the main features of the 1977 Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, and how a constitution is made, amended and reviewed.

mcq.questionText: What is the best meaning of a constitution?

options.text: A set of religious beliefs followed by citizens
The body of fundamental laws and principles by which a country is governed
A list of taxes paid by the people each year
An agreement between two countries to trade goods

mcq.explanation: A constitution is the supreme body of fundamental laws, rules and principles that establishes how a country is governed and how power is shared.

mcq.questionText: A constitution that is written in one single document is called a:
mcq.explanation: A written constitution is contained in a single formal document, such as the Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania of 1977.

mcq.questionText: Which country is most often given as an example of having an unwritten constitution?
mcq.explanation: Britain has an unwritten constitution because its rules are found in many sources such as conventions, customs and various Acts, not in one single document.

mcq.questionText: A constitution that can be changed easily through the same process as ordinary laws is described as:
mcq.explanation: A flexible constitution can be amended easily using the ordinary law-making process, while a rigid constitution requires a special, difficult procedure.

mcq.questionText: In which year was the current Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania adopted?
mcq.explanation: The permanent Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania was adopted in 1977, though it has been amended several times since then.

mcq.questionText: The principle that the constitution is the highest law and that all other laws must agree with it is called:
mcq.explanation: Supremacy of the constitution means it is the highest law of the land; any ordinary law that conflicts with it is void to the extent of that conflict.

mcq.questionText: The part of the constitution that protects the basic rights and freedoms of citizens is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The Bill of Rights is the section of the constitution that guarantees fundamental human rights and duties of citizens.

mcq.questionText: The Bill of Rights was formally added to the Constitution of Tanzania through an amendment in:
mcq.explanation: The Bill of Rights was incorporated into the Constitution through the Fifth Constitutional Amendment of 1984 and became fully enforceable later.

mcq.questionText: The division of government power among the Legislature, the Executive and the Judiciary is called:
mcq.explanation: Separation of powers means dividing government functions among three organs so that no single organ holds all the power.

mcq.questionText: Which organ of government has the main duty of making laws in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: The Legislature, known as Parliament (Bunge), is the organ responsible for making and amending laws.

mcq.questionText: The system whereby each organ of government limits and watches over the others is called:
mcq.explanation: Checks and balances allow each organ of government to limit the powers of the others, preventing abuse of power.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a function or importance of a constitution?

options.text: It defines the powers and duties of government organs
It protects the rights and freedoms of citizens
It sets the daily prices of goods in the market
It guides how leaders are chosen and removed

mcq.explanation: Setting daily market prices is not a function of a constitution; constitutions define government powers, protect rights and guide leadership.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a basic duty of a citizen under the Constitution of Tanzania?

options.text: To refuse to pay any taxes
To obey the law and defend the nation
To take the law into one's own hands

mcq.explanation: The Constitution requires citizens to obey the law, protect public property, pay lawful taxes and defend the nation.

mcq.questionText: A constitution that is difficult to amend and requires a special procedure such as a special majority is called:
mcq.explanation: A rigid constitution needs a special, more difficult procedure to amend, such as a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

mcq.questionText: Which document came BEFORE the permanent 1977 Constitution as a temporary governing law of Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: After the Union of 1964, the Interim Constitution of 1965 governed the country until the permanent Constitution was adopted in 1977.

fib.questionText: A constitution that is contained in many sources and not in one single document is called an _____ constitution.
fib.explanation: An unwritten constitution is found in several sources such as conventions and customs rather than one document, as in Britain.

fib.questionText: The current permanent Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania was adopted in the year _____.
fib.explanation: The permanent Constitution of Tanzania came into force in 1977.

fib.questionText: The principle that the constitution is the highest law of the land is called the _____ of the constitution.
fib.explanation: Supremacy of the constitution means all other laws must conform to it.

fib.questionText: The part of the constitution that lists the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens is called the Bill of _____.
fib.explanation: The Bill of Rights protects citizens' fundamental rights and freedoms.

fib.questionText: The three main organs of government are the Legislature, the Judiciary and the _____.
fib.explanation: The Executive implements laws and runs the day-to-day government, alongside the Legislature and Judiciary.

fib.questionText: The Tanzanian Parliament, which makes laws, is known in Kiswahili as the _____.
fib.explanation: Bunge is the Kiswahili name for the Parliament of Tanzania, the law-making organ.

fib.questionText: A constitution that can be amended easily using the ordinary law-making process is called a _____ constitution.
fib.explanation: A flexible constitution is easy to change, unlike a rigid one which needs a special procedure.

fib.questionText: The organ of government that interprets the law and settles disputes is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Judiciary, made up of the courts, interprets laws and resolves disputes.

fib.questionText: The Bill of Rights was added to the Tanzanian Constitution through the constitutional amendment of the year _____.
fib.explanation: The Bill of Rights was incorporated through the Fifth Constitutional Amendment of 1984.

fib.questionText: The system in which each organ of government limits and controls the powers of the others is known as checks and _____.
fib.explanation: Checks and balances prevent any one organ from abusing its power.

tf.questionText: A constitution is the supreme law of a country and all other laws must agree with it.
tf.explanation: The constitution is supreme, so any ordinary law that conflicts with it is invalid.

tf.questionText: Tanzania has an unwritten constitution like Britain.
tf.explanation: Tanzania has a written constitution, the Constitution of 1977, contained in a single document.

tf.questionText: A rigid constitution is one that can be changed easily through the ordinary law-making process.
tf.explanation: A rigid constitution is difficult to change and needs a special procedure; a flexible one is easy to change.

tf.questionText: The Bill of Rights protects the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens.
tf.explanation: The Bill of Rights guarantees basic rights such as equality, life and freedom of expression.

tf.questionText: Separation of powers means one person should control the Legislature, Executive and Judiciary at the same time.
tf.explanation: Separation of powers divides authority among three organs so that no single person or organ controls all of them.

tf.questionText: The Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania was first adopted in 1961.
tf.explanation: The permanent Constitution was adopted in 1977; 1961 was the year of Tanganyika's independence.

tf.questionText: Paying lawful taxes and obeying the law are duties of citizens under the constitution.
tf.explanation: The constitution lists duties such as obeying the law, paying taxes and defending the nation.

tf.questionText: Checks and balances allow each organ of government to limit the powers of the others.
tf.explanation: Checks and balances stop any organ from abusing its powers by allowing the others to control it.

tf.questionText: Ordinary laws and the constitution have exactly the same legal status in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The constitution is superior to ordinary laws; ordinary laws must conform to the constitution.

tf.questionText: A constitution can be amended to suit the changing needs of society.
tf.explanation: Constitutions can be amended through the proper procedure so they remain relevant to society's changing needs.

summary.correctAnswer: A constitution is the supreme body of fundamental laws, rules and principles by which a country is governed.
summary.explanation: It defines how power is organised and exercised and protects citizens' rights.

summary.questionText: State two types of constitution based on their form.
summary.explanation: A written constitution is in one document; an unwritten one is found in many sources.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between a rigid and a flexible constitution.
summary.correctAnswer: A rigid constitution is hard to change and needs a special procedure, while a flexible one can be changed easily through the ordinary law-making process.
summary.explanation: The difference lies in how easy or difficult the amendment process is.

summary.questionText: Mention two functions of a constitution.
summary.correctAnswer: It defines the powers and duties of government organs and it protects the rights and freedoms of citizens.
summary.explanation: A constitution also guides how leaders are chosen and limits the powers of government.

summary.questionText: What is meant by the supremacy of the constitution?
summary.correctAnswer: It means the constitution is the highest law of the land and all other laws must conform to it.
summary.explanation: Any law that conflicts with the constitution is void to the extent of the conflict.

summary.questionText: Name the three organs of government.
summary.correctAnswer: The Legislature, the Executive and the Judiciary.
summary.explanation: These three organs share government power under the principle of separation of powers.

summary.questionText: What is the Bill of Rights?
summary.correctAnswer: It is the part of the constitution that lists and protects the fundamental rights, freedoms and duties of citizens.
summary.explanation: In Tanzania the Bill of Rights was added through the 1984 amendment.

summary.questionText: Explain the meaning of checks and balances.
summary.correctAnswer: It is a system in which each organ of government limits and controls the powers of the others to prevent abuse of power.
summary.explanation: It works together with separation of powers to protect democracy.

summary.questionText: Give one difference between the constitution and ordinary laws.
summary.correctAnswer: The constitution is the supreme law from which ordinary laws get their validity, while ordinary laws are lower and must conform to the constitution.
summary.explanation: Ordinary laws are usually easier to make and change than the constitution.

summary.questionText: Why is constitutional review or reform important?
summary.correctAnswer: It allows the constitution to be updated to meet the changing needs of society and to improve democracy, rights and governance.
summary.explanation: Tanzania began a constitutional review process leading to the 2014 Proposed Constitution to address such needs.

hoq.questionText: If Parliament passes an ordinary law that contradicts a right protected in the Constitution of Tanzania, what is the most likely outcome and why?

options.text: The new law replaces the constitution because Parliament made it
The new law can be declared void by the courts because the constitution is supreme
Both the law and the constitution become equal in status
Citizens must obey the new law instead of the constitution

hoq.explanation: Because of the supremacy of the constitution, any ordinary law that conflicts with it can be challenged and declared void by the courts.

hoq.questionText: A leader controls the courts, makes the laws and enforces them all by himself. Which constitutional principle is being violated, and what is the danger?

options.text: Supremacy of the constitution; the danger is high taxes
Separation of powers; the danger is dictatorship and abuse of power
The right to vote; the danger is poor roads
Freedom of worship; the danger is unemployment

hoq.explanation: Combining all powers in one person violates separation of powers and can lead to dictatorship and abuse of power, which checks and balances are meant to prevent.

hoq.questionText: Why might a country prefer a rigid written constitution rather than a flexible one for protecting fundamental rights?

options.text: Because a rigid constitution can be changed any day by one minister
Because the difficult amendment procedure makes it harder for leaders to remove rights quickly for their own benefit
Because a rigid constitution has no written rules to follow
Because flexible constitutions cannot protect any rights at all

hoq.explanation: A rigid constitution needs a special, difficult procedure such as a two-thirds majority to amend, so leaders cannot easily strip away citizens' rights, giving stronger protection.
